title: Microsoft Teams: customise the file types blocked by Weaponizable File Protection
summary: The briefing's rollout dates, default behaviour and configuration controls are supported by Microsoft's notice, roadmap record and Learn documentation. It correctly distinguishes the optional custom list from the existing protection switch and does not promise unpublished licensing.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to let administrators customise the extensions blocked by Teams Weaponizable File Protection or retain the recommended list.
claims.quote: Administrators will be able to customize which file types are blocked in Teams to align with their organization's security requirements or continue using the Microsoft-recommended default list.

claims.claim: The MicrosoftTeams cmdlet Set-CsTeamsMessagingConfiguration supports -FileTypeCustomizationSetting CustomBlockList -FileTypeBlockList <string[]> to set the custom list.
claims.quote: CustomBlockList: Blocks the file types you specify in the FileTypeBlockList parameter instead of the Microsoft-recommended list.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMessagingConfiguration -FileTypeCustomizationSetting MicrosoftRecommendedBlockList selects the recommended list.
claims.quote: MicrosoftRecommendedBlockList: Blocks the file types on the Microsoft-recommended list. This keeps the existing behavior.

claims.claim: The protection switch is in Teams admin center > Messaging settings > Messaging safety > Scan messages for file types that are not allowed.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation, select Messaging settings.
3. Scroll down to Messaging safety settings.
4. Turn on the setting: Scan messages for file types that are not allowed.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMessagingConfiguration supports -FileTypeCheck with Enabled or Disabled and the -Identity parameter for the protection switch.
claims.quote:
This setting enables weaponizable file detection in Teams messages in the tenant.

Possible Values:

- Enabled
- Disabled

claims.claim: No per-user or per-group blocked-extension list control is documented on either surface.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Weaponizable File Protection custom block list per user group policy FileTypeBlockList. Opened: Weaponizable File Protection in Microsoft Teams; Set-CsTeamsMessagingConfiguration. The reference describes a single global tenant configuration, not user or group lists.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Teams scans messages to identify files with weaponizable extensions and blocks messages when a blocked type is detected.
claims.quote:
Teams automatically scans the message and identifies files with weaponizable extensions.
3. If a blocked file type is detected, Teams prevents the message from being delivered and displays appropriate notifications to both sender and recipients.

claims.claim: Both the attachment and the complete message content are blocked.
claims.quote: If you send a message containing a weaponizable file, both the file attachment and the complete message content are blocked.

claims.claim: The sender can edit the original message to remove the unsafe file and resend it.
claims.quote:
Have the option to edit the original message to remove the unsafe file.
- Resend the message once the problematic file is removed.
